rv.q: It's a great idea, but it needs an onstage raison d'être... to begin with this is a pretty laboured set-up.
What we get is a jokey travesty that leads me to agree with Gwendolen that: 'On an occasion of this kind it becomes more than a moral duty to speak one's mind. It becomes a pleasure.'

More generally, though, the effect is one of quiet, inward and constant delight in the audience rather than any rolling in the aisles – and what could be more revelatory than that in a classic we all think we know so well?
The whole production is so odd that it stops it being funny and THE IMPORTANCE OF BEING EARNEST is usually a very funny play indeed.

cn.t: Critics find this reimagined production with veteran actors misguided, with the framing device of a play-within-a-play undermining Wilde's comedy rather than enhancing it, though some appreciate the experienced cast's efforts.
